title: Étale origin of constructible complexes locally of finite Tor dimension
statement:
Let $X$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], and let $A$ be a discrete commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Use the small étale and pro-étale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], constant coefficient sheaves $A_X$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], categories of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $\nu_X:X_{\mathrm{proét}}\to X_{\mathrm{ét}}$ for the comparison morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] and $\nu_X^*$ for its inverse image on module sheaves, which is exact [det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules] and is applied termwise on derived categories.

For $M\in D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},A_X)$, the following are equivalent:

1. Every $H^q(M)$ is constructible [def-sfb-affine-locally-constructible-proetale-modules], and $M$ locally has finite Tor dimension: for every site object $U$ there is a covering $\{U_i\to U\}$ and integers $a_i\leq b_i$ such that $H^q(M|_{U_i}\otimes^L_{A_X|_{U_i}}N_i)=0$ for every degree-zero module sheaf $N_i$ on the slice and every $q\notin[a_i,b_i]$. Slice restriction is [def-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-restriction, def-pur-localized-ringed-site], and the K-flat derived tensor product over the constant ring sheaf and cohomology are [def-weil-derived-tensor, def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude, def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves].
2. There are a bounded constructible complex $C\in D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{ét}},A)$ [def-pe-etale-constructible-module] and an isomorphism $\nu_X^*C\simeq M$, with $C$ of finite Tor amplitude: there exist integers $a\leq b$ such that $H^q(C\otimes^L_{A_X}N)=0$ (étale K-flat derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor]) for every degree-zero étale $A_X$-module sheaf $N$ and every $q\notin[a,b]$.

No boundedness, completeness, or prior étale-origin assumption is imposed on $M$.

source.place: Tag 09C2, lemma-describe-constructible-complexes, parts (2) and (4) for n=1 and their proof (the uniform Tor interval on quasi-compact X, and étale origin via Tag 09AL, lemma-compare-constructible-derived, with the 'small argument omitted' that the étale antecedent keeps the Tor interval); the converse direction from Tag 09AL and the Noetherian interval comparison.

proof.text: Apply lem-sfb-proetale-tor-local-global to turn the local finite Tor condition into one ordered global Tor interval [a,b], including on the empty scheme.

Apply lem-pe-coefficient-tor-flat-model to the global interval. It gives a cochain representative P with flat terms that is zero below a and above b. Its cohomology vanishes outside [a,b]; the homology localization factorization and the representative isomorphism identify this with the cohomology of M. Together with the assumed constructibility, M is bounded constructible. This reuses the existing flat-model criterion, whose proof already includes the unit tensor test, rather than introducing a new boundedness lemma.

Use the restricted finite-Tor equivalence in det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian, which is the restriction of sk-thm-pe-constructible-comparison. Apply its inverse to the bounded constructible finite-Tor object M. The resulting etale object C is bounded constructible and has a finite Tor interval by its full-subcategory property. The natural isomorphism identifying the forward functor with derived comparison, followed by the equivalence counit, gives D(C) isomorphic to M. Choose a representative P using essential surjectivity of the standard localization Q. The localization factorization Q followed by D is naturally isomorphic to termwise comparison followed by Q; composing its component at P, D applied to Q(P) isomorphic to C, and D(C) isomorphic to M gives precisely the required termwise representative isomorphism.

Conversely, factor the given representative isomorphism through D using the localization factorization and the isomorphism Q(P) to C. Regard C as an object of the finite-Tor bounded constructible etale subcategory. The forward finite-Tor equivalence gives a bounded constructible finite-Tor pro-etale object, and its prescribed comparison identifies it with M. Transport constructibility degreewise using lem-pe-coefficient-constructible-iso; transport the same cohomological vanishing interval using functoriality of cohomology. Transport its Tor interval by composing every K-flat representative isomorphism with the derived isomorphism. Finally apply the global-to-local direction of lem-sfb-proetale-tor-local-global.

proof_origin.place: Tags 09C2 and 09AL, lemma-describe-constructible-complexes and lemma-compare-constructible-derived. Boundedness reuses the coefficient flat-model criterion (Tags 08G0 and 08G1); descent and Tor reflection use the already restricted finite-Tor comparison equivalence. Lean proof by T8, 2026-10-21.

lean.statement: theorem constructible_localTor_iff_etaleOrigin (X : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] (A : Type (max v (u + 1))) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (M : ConstantCompletion.D (ConstantCompletion.constant (Scheme.coefficientProEtaleModelTopology.{u, v} X) A)) : ((∀ q : ℤ, Scheme.IsCoefficientAffineLocallyConstructibleProEtaleModuleSheaf X A ((coefficientModelCohomology _ q).obj M)) ∧ ∀ U : Scheme.coefficientProEtaleSiteModel.{u, v} X, ∃ S : Presieve U, Sieve.generate S ∈ Scheme.coefficientProEtaleModelTopology.{u, v} X U ∧ ∀ (V : Scheme.coefficientProEtaleSiteModel.{u, v} X) (f : V ⟶ U), S f → ∃ a b : ℤ, HasCoefficientModelTorAmplitude ((ConstantCompletion.constant (Scheme.coefficientProEtaleModelTopology.{u, v} X) A).over V) ((coefficientModelSliceRestriction (ConstantCompletion.constant (Scheme.coefficientProEtaleModelTopology.{u, v} X) A) V).obj M) a b) ↔ ∃ C : ConstantCompletion.D (ConstantCompletion.constant (Scheme.smallModelComparisonEtaleTopology.{u, v} X) A), Scheme.IsCoefficientBoundedConstructibleEtale X A C ∧ (∃ a b : ℤ, HasCoefficientModelTorAmplitude _ C a b) ∧ ∃ P : ConstantCompletion.Cx (ConstantCompletion.constant (Scheme.smallModelComparisonEtaleTopology.{u, v} X) A), Nonempty ((ConstantCompletion.Q _).obj P ≅ C) ∧ Nonempty ((ConstantCompletion.Q _).obj ((constructibleComparisonComplexPullback X A).obj P) ≅ M)
lean.note: The canonical derived inverse image is expressed termwise: an unbounded cochain representative P with Q(P) isomorphic to C and Q(constructibleComparisonComplexPullback(P)) isomorphic to M. Exactness and localization identify this with nu_X^* C, independently of the representative; no origin or boundedness hypothesis is imposed on M. Uses the existing coefficient-sized site models, cohomology and universal K-flat Tor tests.
